newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ERA says uranium prices to hurt profits.
newsitem.headline: ERA says uranium prices to hurt profits.

text.p: Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, which mines about 7.5 percent of the world's market for uranium, said on Tuesday low metal prices would weigh on net profits in the 1996-97 year ended June 30.
"This year we won't repeat last year's figure," ERA chief executive Phillip Shirvington told reporters at the company's Ranger uranium mine.
In 1995/96 ERA posted a net profit of A$40 million.
ERA will record its 1996/97 profit statement around August 21 or 22, a company spokeswoman said.
Uranium prices traded at between US$13 and US$18 a lb in 1996/97, forced down because large utility customers had large stocks, Shirvington said.
Spot uranium prices have started off 1997-98 at only US$10.50 a lb, which could also hit current year profits, Shirvington added.

An Australian federal court ruling due this week that threatens to halt potential exports of uranium by ERA from its proposed Jabiluka uranium mine near its main Ranger One and Three orebodies would probably be delayed for further hearings, Shirvington said.
Some Aboriginal groups that live near the mine have claimed that the Jabiluka mining lease is invalid and have taken their claim to federal court.
ERA, 68.4-percent owned by diversified resources group North Ltd, should produce about 5,000 tonnes of uranium oxide in the current year.
About 60 percent of ERA's uranium is sold under long-term contracts to utilities in Asia and Europe. The rest is exposed to world spot prices.
